description: Deliver the RESEARCH LOOP harness (the user's core ask: a loop where the agent can directly look at results and iterate on strategies), the HONEST PARITY documentation (README), and the Round 5 ITERATION_LOG.md entry. The research loop ties FEAT-001..003 together into a repeatable batch: run one-or-many strategy/param configs on a data slice, rank them by the tuner score (hard 15% relative-DD ceiling), print a leaderboard + diagnosis, and persist results as JSON so the agent can read them back, propose a new config, and re-run - closing the develop->measure->rank->iterate loop entirely in-sandbox. Depends on FEAT-001..003. STDLIB ONLY, pure ASCII, Python 3.9+.
steps: RESEARCH HARNESS python_bt/research.py with `python3 -m python_bt.research` entry: a driver that takes a list of candidate configs (each = {strategy_name, params, label}) from a JSON/py file or the built-in default set, runs each through the engine on a chosen data slice (shared --from/--to/--mode/--max-ticks flags mirroring runner.py), collects {label, metrics, score, meta}, RANKS by score() descending (respecting the hard DD ceiling so any config over 15% relative DD sinks below every compliant one), and prints a LEADERBOARD (label, net profit, relative DD %, profit factor, trades, score, and the analyzer diagnosis verdict per config). Persist all results to a JSON file (e.g. reports/pybt/<timestamp>.results.json - create the dir; note reports/*.summary.json is gitignored but this path is a new subdir, so either write under reports/pybt/ and add a .gitignore note, or write under python_bt/results/ - choose a path that is NOT accidentally committed as a big file; results JSON are tiny so committing is fine but keep it small). The point: the agent runs research.py, reads the JSON leaderboard, forms a hypothesis, edits/adds a config or a new Strategy subclass, and re-runs - a tight in-sandbox iteration loop. Include a --top N to show only the best N and a --baseline flag to always include GaganStrategy defaults for comparison.

MAKE IT EASY TO ADD STRATEGIES: ensure research.py can discover configs from a simple JSON file (list of {strategy, params, label}) passed via --configs @file.json, so the agent iterates by editing that file, and can also reference any registered Strategy by name. Document in README how to add a brand-new strategy (subclass Strategy, register, add a config entry) and re-run research.py.

PARITY README python_bt/README.md (pure ASCII, no em dashes): the crux of trustworthiness. Sections: (1) What this is - a fast in-sandbox research rig for XAUUSD strategies; MT5 is the SOURCE OF TRUTH. (2) Layout - list every module and its role. (3) How to run - extract data (python3 data/extract.py), run the runner CLI, run the research loop, add a strategy. (4) The DEVELOP->MEASURE->RANK->ITERATE loop and how the agent participates. (5) PARITY ASSUMPTIONS (each flagged CONFIRM): POINT_SIZE=0.01 (detected from 2-decimal XAUUSD quotes), CONTRACT_SIZE=100 oz, TICK_SIZE=0.01, TICK_VALUE per lot, COMMISSION_PER_LOT_PER_SIDE (Fusion), INITIAL_DEPOSIT=1000, LEVERAGE 1:500, spread source = per-tick ask-bid, fill timing = next tick / bar close, no requotes, slippage model = none (or state fixed), how partial closes / breakeven / trailing are simulated, how ATR/RSI/EMA are seeded, how H1 HTF EMA is built. (6) KNOWN DIFFERENCES vs MT5 (bar-close vs intra-bar timing, indicator seeding, swap not modeled unless added, margin/leverage not enforced, spread realism, no news gaps). (7) A blunt statement: Python results MUST be validated against a real MT5 run of the same period before being trusted; the Python engine is for FAST SEARCH, MT5 is authoritative. (8) How the metrics + score map to tools/analyze_report.py and automation/tuner/scoring.py so results are comparable across the MT5 path and the Python path.
